sheets.name: README
rows: Traceability view for one regulation-to-SHACL generation run.
Generation is frozen before RDF execution; no ship graph or hidden expected outcome is used here.
events.jsonl is append-only; CSV and Excel sheets are derived views.
Static validation passed and the semantic validator accepted the candidate.
No verified canonical term was available; the generator was not allowed to invent one.
Accepted shapes await the separate bulk evaluator.

sheets.name: RUNS
rows: Remove sh:minCount 1 from the selectedHullAreaFactor property. The requirement is conditional on a structural member having spanned hull-area values, and the supplied hasSpannedHullArea path already supplies applicability; requiring a selected result for every structural member invents an existence constraint and can create an accidental failure for members with no applicable path. Retain the expected-result-scaled tolerance and operand-exceeds-selected rejection in the calculation check.

rows: Replace the exact numeric equality logic in the maximum-selection SPARQL check. selectedHullAreaFactor is a derived decimal result, so validate it against the expected maximum hullAreaFactor with a scaled tolerance based on that expected maximum (not on the reported selected value), while retaining rejection when any operand exceeds the selected value. Do not add invented applicability or existence constraints; the existing hasSpannedHullArea path supplies applicability.

Replace the SPARQL ABS calls in the derived-maximum check. DIRECT_CALCULATION permits only the registered arithmetic, comparisons, min/max, and simple piecewise operations; express the expected-result-scaled tolerance using supported arithmetic and a piecewise sign branch (or an equivalent supported form), while retaining rejection when any hullAreaFactor operand exceeds selectedHullAreaFactor. The prior requirement to base tolerance on the expected maximum, not the reported value, is otherwise satisfied.

Repair the derived-maximum SPARQL check. Remove the standalone `?expected > ?reported` rejection: it rejects every reported value below the expected maximum, so the permitted tolerance is not applied symmetrically. Compare the reported result only against `?expected - ?tol` and `?expected + ?tol`, where `?tol` is scaled from the expected result (positive: `?expected * 0.000001`; negative: `(-?expected) * 0.000001`; zero or near zero: `0.000001`). The current lower bound also incorrectly uses a fixed absolute tolerance for negative expected values; use the same expected-scaled tolerance on both sides. Retain the rejection when another spanned factor exceeds the selected value, and preserve the existing path-based applicability without adding existence or applicability constraints.

Remove sh:minCount 1 from the selectedHullAreaFactor property. The requirement is conditional on a structural member having spanned hull-area values, and the supplied hasSpannedHullArea path already supplies applicability; requiring a selected result for every structural member invents an existence constraint and can create an accidental failure for members with no applicable path. Retain the expected-result-scaled tolerance and operand-exceeds-selected rejection in the calculation check.
